KNKX vs KSOX: profile examples

Blue: KNKX observed. Orange: KSOX observed. Dashed green: KSOX extrapolated using the with-AGL model.

Left: simultaneous scans (within 3 minutes). Right: a lag based on measured flight speed and direction (within 3 minutes of that shifted time). Both columns use the same KSOX profile and axis scales. Heights are metres above sea level; times are Pacific local time. The night date refers to the evening.

Gray shading is below KSOX’s lowest measured layer. The stations are 114 km apart, with KNKX’s antenna 625 m lower. These are regional comparisons, not measurements of exactly the same airspace.

These six examples have plausible movement directions and both scan matches available. They were chosen for agreement in the observed upper layers, without using lower-layer prediction errors. All 40 nights and methods.

Spring

Night of 2016-05-02

KNKX movement: 13.2 m/s toward 301°. KSOX: 11.7 m/s toward 311°. Lag: 171 minutes, with KNKX first.

The simultaneous pairing supplied the upper-layer match used to select this example.
